acceptance.given: An external process execution is running under the bounded Toolchain replay executor.

oracle.expected: The terminal observation records one deterministic terminal state for the process, with timeout or budget exhaustion represented as unsuccessful.
forbidden: The process terminal state is indeterminate or nondeterministic.
Budget exhaustion is treated as success or reduces required coverage.
oracle.observable: At the end of the execution, the process receipt contains a deterministic terminal category and bounded execution outcome.

acceptance.then: The receipt and validator check identify the same deterministic terminal state and reject any indeterminate, unbounded, or budget-success outcome.
acceptance.when: The S11 runtime test invokes the external process and evaluates its terminal receipt.

failure_intents.selector_intent: S11 test demonstrates an external process whose terminal observation is missing, ambiguous, or budget-exhausted and verifies the runtime marker is unsuccessful.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce bounded external-process execution and deterministic terminal-state classification; timeout or output-budget exhaustion remains unsuccessful.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing terminal categories and receipt schema; rollback restores prior bounded-executor behavior.

slice_hint.state_transition: executing -> deterministically terminal (pass, execution-failed, or timed-out); budget exhaustion transitions to unsuccessful.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: S11 completes only when a bounded receipt names exactly one deterministic terminal category and marks timeout/budget exhaustion unsuccessful.

acceptance.given: A TC-D1 Toolchain write request targets a user-sandbox boundary.

oracle.expected: The write is rejected and no user-sandbox path is modified or authorized by replay or Consumer permission.
forbidden: Replay or Consumer permission is treated as authorization for user-sandbox repair.
oracle.observable: The governance check emits a rejection and the attempted target remains outside the Toolchain write set.

acceptance.then: The boundary validator records a denied write with the target classified as user-sandbox and preserves the Toolchain-only write scope.
acceptance.when: The SM-6 boundary test evaluates the attempted write during the S36 replay/source-identity validation invocation.

failure_intents.selector_intent: S36 test supplies a user-sandbox target to the Toolchain write boundary and verifies the target-binding guard fails closed.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Reject any TC-D1 Toolchain write targeting user-sandbox boundaries; replay and Consumer permission cannot widen the Toolchain write scope.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Keep replay receipt and write-boundary schemas compatible; rollback restores the prior deny-by-default Toolchain boundary.

slice_hint.state_transition: proposed Toolchain write -> boundary classification -> rejected when target is user-sandbox.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: S36 is terminal only when a user-sandbox target yields an explicit rejection and no authorized write action.

acceptance.given: The six Matrix Cases are scheduled for execution with immutable Stable and Candidate subjects.

oracle.expected: Execution inputs and evidence identify distinct fixtures and state for Stable versus Candidate in every Matrix Case.
forbidden: Stable and Candidate use shared fixtures.
Stable and Candidate share mutable execution state or indistinguishable evidence.
oracle.observable: The S7 matrix receipt records separate fixture/state identities for Stable and Candidate executions.

acceptance.then: The matrix validator confirms Stable and Candidate fixture/state identities are distinct and attributable for each case.
acceptance.when: The S7 matrix test executes all Matrix Cases and inspects the resulting fixture/state bindings.

failure_intents.selector_intent: S7 test intentionally binds Stable and Candidate to the same fixture or mutable state and verifies the separation constraint is rejected.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require immutable Stable and Candidate subjects to execute each Matrix Case with distinct fixtures, state, and attributable evidence.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve matrix receipt fields and existing Stable/Candidate identity formats while restoring prior isolated execution semantics.

slice_hint.state_transition: matrix case scheduled -> isolated Stable execution and isolated Candidate execution -> attributable paired evidence.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: S7 is terminal only when every Matrix Case has two completed executions whose fixture and state identities are unequal and independently attributable.

acceptance.given: An aggregate evaluation is presented with matrix evidence whose freshness check reports stale inputs.

oracle.expected: The aggregate is marked invalid and cannot be accepted when matrix evidence is stale.
forbidden: The stale aggregate is accepted or promoted.
oracle.observable: The S24 evaluation receipt contains an invalid/stale verdict and acceptance is refused.

acceptance.then: The aggregate evaluator refuses acceptance and records the stale-evidence invalidation category.
acceptance.when: The S24 integration test injects stale matrix evidence and evaluates the aggregate freshness gate.

failure_intents.selector_intent: S24 test presents stale matrix evidence and verifies that an aggregate incorrectly accepted as valid is reported as an unexpected green.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Invalidate and refuse acceptance of any aggregate whose matrix evidence is stale, copied, mislabeled, missing, or otherwise freshness-invalid.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve aggregate verdict categories and stale-evidence fields; rollback restores prior freshness validation without accepting stale evidence.

slice_hint.state_transition: aggregate evaluated with matrix evidence -> freshness check stale -> aggregate invalid and acceptance blocked.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: S24 is terminal only when stale matrix evidence yields an invalid aggregate verdict and no acceptance publication path is available.
